items.headline: Greed stays at 75 and Valuation at 87; PRICE_DISCIPLINE remains active
items.summary: The AGCI live engine reads Greed 75/100 and Valuation 87/100, with regime Correction and condition PRICE_DISCIPLINE — Wait / Price discipline. The underlying market inputs remain primarily from the September 11 close, so no artificial weekend score change is inferred.
items.whyItMatters: Valuation remains extreme while macro and energy risk have risen. The portfolio implication remains selective risk-taking rather than chasing beta or long duration.

items.headline: Major global banks converge on a September Fed hike as markets price roughly 90% odds
items.category: Macro / Central Banks / Rates / Capital Allocation
items.summary: Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, HSBC and Deutsche Bank now expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates by 25 basis points at the September 15–16 meeting after stronger August inflation and the renewed oil shock. Reuters reported market pricing near a 90% probability of a hike, up from roughly 70% before the latest inflation data.
items.whyItMatters: The hurdle rate for equities, real estate and long-duration bonds has moved higher. AGCI should treat any pre-Fed risk rally cautiously and preserve staggered duration rather than front-running easing.
items.agciSignal: FED HIKE BASE CASE / HIGHER-FOR-LONGER RISK / STAGGER DURATION

items.headline: Hormuz commodity traffic remains severely depressed as the Saudi bypass stays impaired
items.summary: Reuters reported that only four commodity vessels exited and ten entered the Gulf through Hormuz over the weekend, well below recent traffic and far below pre-war activity. The slowdown follows repeated shipping incidents while Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remains shut after a drone attack.
items.whyItMatters: The energy shock remains physical rather than purely headline-driven. Restricted maritime flows plus a compromised bypass increase upside risk to crude, diesel, freight, insurance and inflation.
items.agciSignal: PHYSICAL ENERGY DISRUPTION / HEDGE MODERATE / DO NOT CHASE

items.headline: Oman postpones Gulf-Iran Hormuz meeting with no replacement date
items.summary: Oman postponed the regional meeting that had been scheduled for September 14 to discuss possible arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi cited the need for consensus; no new date was announced.
items.whyItMatters: The near-term diplomatic off-ramp weakened. AGCI should not price an imminent normalization of Gulf shipping until there is a rescheduled process, a binding framework and visible recovery in physical flows.

items.newsletter: Barron's — AI Slowdown and the Tech Selloff / 14 Sep 2026
items.headline: AI safety warnings trigger a broad tech de-risking move ahead of the Fed
items.summary: Barron's highlighted an AI-linked technology selloff, while Reuters reported that warnings from leading AI executives about slowing development pressured global AI stocks and Nasdaq futures. Nvidia and AMD were among the names under pressure in early trading indications.
items.whyItMatters: This is a valuation and duration stress test for the AI complex, not evidence that end-demand has disappeared. AGCI should separate safety/regulatory sentiment from contracted compute demand, utilization, financing quality, margins and free cash flow.
items.agciSignal: AI VOLATILITY UP / KEEP QUALITY FILTER / NO PANIC BUYING

items.headline: Fed decision, housing and retail define the next U.S. catalyst set
items.summary: The authorized Barron's Daily Roundup flagged the September Fed decision, housing data, retail indicators and Lennar as the principal scheduled catalysts for the week. These are forward-looking watch items rather than new confirmed allocation signals.
items.whyItMatters: Housing and retail will help determine how much the higher-rate and energy shock is reaching the real economy. AGCI keeps real-estate stress assumptions unchanged until fresh data or company results justify an adjustment.
items.agciSignal: CATALYST WATCH / NO THESIS CHANGE YET

watch: Fed September 15–16: decision, dot/guidance and whether the market's roughly 90% hike probability is validated.
Treasury 10Y: test of the 5% area and transmission into mortgage rates, cap rates and equity duration.
Saudi East-West pipeline: repair timeline, effective export losses and depletion of Red Sea inventories.
Hormuz: vessel counts, attacks, insurance, diesel and freight; require physical normalization before reducing the hedge.
Oman diplomacy: rescheduling of the Gulf-Iran meeting and whether a binding navigation framework emerges.
AI complex: distinguish safety/regulatory headlines from contracted demand, utilization, counterparty quality, margin and FCF.
Housing/real estate: Lennar, home sales and mortgage-rate transmission; retain +50/+100 bp stress until evidence changes.
Mexico-U.S./USMCA: no new official material decision in this cut; keep monitoring autos, Section 232, rules of origin and Chinese investment screening.
Travel: Gulf, Hormuz, Saudi Arabia and Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb remain very high operational risk.
